purpose: Evidence that selected architecture families have manufacturer product precedents; not an industrial-coverage census or a benchmark/reference-solution set.

scope_boundary.maximum_four_stages: A proposed library boundary; not an industry-wide maximum. The SEW P family explicitly also contains five-stage products.
scope_boundary.hundreds_of_combinations: A design target or hypothesis requiring a declared component alphabet, connection rules, canonicalization, feasibility filters, and a counted generated inventory.
scope_boundary.all_have_industrial_applications: Not established. Family-level evidence cannot prove that every enumerated ordering, connection, or parameter range has an installed industrial example.
scope_boundary.stage_count_policy: Must be defined by the architecture owner before counting. A planetary stage must not automatically be counted as two serial stages because it contains two mesh types. Transmission stage count is not the number of selectable automotive gear ratios.

entries.verified_family_precedent: A helical-and-worm compound family is currently offered; a manufacturer technical note documents the base path as helical first, worm second.
entries.stage_count_qualification: Two-stage path is explicitly documented in the July 2003 technical note. It is not a statement that every current S compound variant has only two stages.
entries.proposed_library_use: Precedent for a directed helical-to-worm chain, with direction-specific loss/backdrive and thermal models still to be established for a candidate.
entries.application_area_evidence: The current product page lists machine/plant uses including adjustment drives, presses, and rotary tables; these are application categories.
unknowns: Stage count of an added primary reducer

entries.product_family: P series planetary units with primary helical/bevel-helical gearmotors
entries.verified_family_precedent: The manufacturer combines an upstream helical or bevel-helical gearmotor with planetary units.
entries.stage_count_qualification: P.RF is listed as four/five stage, P.KF as five stage. A four-stage library may admit only explicitly qualified four-stage variants.
entries.verified_input_to_output_order: primary helical or bevel-helical gearmotor -> planetary unit; individual internal stage sequence is not specified by the family page
entries.proposed_library_use: Family-level precedent for serial mixed gearing and direct counterevidence to a universal four-stage industrial limit.
entries.application_area_evidence: The page discusses slow process equipment such as mixers and rotary filters, without identifying a named customer installation.
unknowns: Exact stage decomposition per selected variant

entries.product_family: P-X.e planetary units with primary X.e bevel-helical units
entries.verified_family_precedent: A standardized mixed family combines a primary X.e bevel-helical unit with a P/P2.e planetary unit.
entries.stage_count_qualification: Counts are stated in the product-family table, not reconstructed from a complete internal drawing.
entries.verified_input_to_output_order: primary X.e bevel-helical unit -> P/P2.e planetary unit; exact stage-level decomposition remains variant-specific
entries.proposed_library_use: Precedent for a mixed right-angle and planetary architecture within a three-/four-stage subset.
entries.application_area_evidence: The manufacturer lists conveyors, shredders, presses, mixers and other application categories.

entries.product_family: MAXXDRIVE XC / XD parallel helical industrial gear units
entries.verified_family_precedent: Parallel helical products include XC two-/three-stage and XD three-/four-stage configurations.
entries.stage_count_qualification: Stage options belong to the identified XC or XD subfamily; they are not interchangeable configuration guarantees.
entries.verified_input_to_output_order: multi-stage parallel helical family; individual internal shaft connections are not specified here
entries.proposed_library_use: Precedent for two- through four-stage parallel-axis chains; detailed candidate geometry still requires its own evidence.
entries.application_area_evidence: The page includes lifting uses and an unnamed Moroccan phosphate-mine conveyor example. The latter is a vendor-reported anonymous installation, not a fully identified OEM case.
unknowns: Stage count of the reported mine drive
Actual conveyor load, distinct from catalog maximum

entries.verified_family_precedent: The planetary-family ratio table offers one-, two-, and three-stage configurations, with availability depending on frame size.
entries.stage_count_qualification: The source confirms multi-stage planetary options, including two-stage, rather than proving a particular differential or compound-planetary construction.
entries.verified_input_to_output_order: coaxial multi-stage planetary family; exact per-stage member connections require a drawing or manual
entries.proposed_library_use: Precedent for repeated planetary stages. It cannot validate every ring-fixed, sun-driven, carrier-output library arrangement without further documents.
entries.application_area_evidence: The page refers to demanding production cycles, without a named customer installation.
unknowns: Exact member connections and tooth counts

coverage_claims_allowed: Selected multi-stage parallel-axis, mixed helical/worm, mixed primary-gearing/planetary, and repeated-planetary product families have manufacturer precedents.
The evidence is sufficient to justify treating these as engineering-relevant families for a proposed library.
coverage_claims_not_allowed: Every generated combination has an industrial installation.
Industry generally stops at four stages.
Hundreds of canonical feasible topologies have already been demonstrated or counted.
Catalog maximum torque is an installed load case.
A manufacturer family page is a validated numerical reference solution.
Stage count equals automotive gear/shift count.
